title: Grammar: Word Formation — Noun and Verb Suffixes
grammarTip:
Словообразование (Word formation) — как строить новые слова:

СУФФИКСЫ существительных:
-tion/-sion: investigate→investigation · contribute→contribution
-ment: develop→development · manage→management
-ness: aware→awareness · effective→effectiveness
-ity: responsible→responsibility · flexible→flexibility
-er/-or: research→researcher · instruct→instructor

СУФФИКСЫ прилагательных:
-ful: success→successful · help→helpful
-less: use→useless · care→careless
-ive: effect→effective · create→creative
-able/-ible: rely→reliable · access→accessible
-al: tradition→traditional · economy→economical

ПРЕФИКСЫ:
un- = отрицание: unsuccessful · unreliable
mis- = неправильно: misunderstand · misinterpret
pre- = до: predict · prepare
over- = слишком: overestimate · overlook

grammarTable.subject: -tion / -sion
grammarTable.example: invest → investment? NO: invest → investment; but: distribute → distribution; regulate → regulation; inflate → inflation

grammarTable.subject: -ment
grammarTable.example: employ → employment; govern → government; develop → development; manage → management

grammarTable.subject: -er / -or / -ist
grammarTable.example: invest → investor; consume → consumer; produce → producer; manage → manager; economy → economist

grammarTable.subject: -ity / -ness
grammarTable.example: equal → equality; stable → stability; scarce → scarcity; productive → productivity; aware → awareness

grammarTable.subject: -ance / -ence
grammarTable.example: perform → performance; depend → dependence; compete → competition; prefer → preference; influ→ influence

grammarTable.subject: -ise / -ize
grammarTable.example: private → privatise; global → globalise; stable → stabilise; capital → capitalise; modern → modernise

rows.form: Most common pattern for economic/academic nouns
rows.example: regulate → regulation; distribute → distribution; consume → consumption; produce → production; allocate → allocation

rows.form: Verb endings affect the spelling: -te drops to -tion
rows.example: inflate → inflation; investigate → investigation; appreciate → appreciation

rows.form: -ss + ion: express → expression; oppress → oppression
rows.example: compress → compression; possess → possession; access → accession

rows.form: Note irregular forms to memorise
rows.example: grow → growth (not growtion!); lose → loss; choose → choice; solve → solution

rows.form: verb + -ment = noun (result or state of the verb)
rows.example: employ → employment; invest → investment; achieve → achievement; govern → government

rows.form: Common in economics and policy language
rows.example: develop → development; manage → management; adjust → adjustment; improve → improvement

rows.form: Sometimes the base form changes slightly
rows.example: judge → judgement (or judgment); move → movement

rows.form: Note: NOT all verbs take -ment (must learn individually)
rows.example: consume → consumption (not "consumement"); produce → production (not "producement")

rows.form: -er = most common (person who does the verb)
rows.example: manage → manager; borrow → borrower; save → saver; spend → spender; lead → leader

rows.form: -or = formal/Latin origin verbs
rows.example: invest → investor; regulate → regulator; direct → director; supervise → supervisor

rows.form: -ist = person who follows an idea or discipline
rows.example: economy → economist; capital → capitalist; social → socialist; specialism → specialist

rows.form: Some have multiple forms with different meanings
rows.example: compete → competitor (in a market); compete → competence (skill) — NOT "competer"

rows.form: noun/adj + -ise/-ize = to make or become
rows.example: global → globalise/globalize; private → privatise/privatize; stable → stabilise/stabilize

rows.form: Very productive in economics and policy
rows.example: modern → modernise; liberal → liberalise; national → nationalise; computer → computerise

rows.form: BrE spelling: -ise; AmE: -ize (both acceptable in B1)
rows.example: "privatise" (BrE) = "privatize" (AmE) — same meaning

rows.form: Some verbs: noun + -ify (alternative pattern)
rows.example: simple → simplify; class → classify; identity → identify; diversity → diversify

rows.form: economy, economic, economical, economically, economist, economics
rows.example: "An economist studies the economic policies of nations to understand if they are economical."

rows.form: invest, investor, investment, investable, investing
rows.example: "Investors evaluate investment opportunities based on their risk and return."

rows.form: produce, producer, product, production, productive, productively, productivity
rows.example: "High productivity enables producers to increase production without higher costs."

rows.form: distribute, distributor, distribution, distributive
rows.example: "Distribution of income affects distributive justice and social equality."

exercises.text: "The ___ of income between different groups has become more unequal." (distribute)

exercises.instruction: Form the noun from the verb.
exercises.text: "___ in renewable energy has increased significantly." (invest)
"The ___ in this market faces stiff competition from abroad." (produce)
exercises.hint: produce → producer (-er suffix: person who produces)

exercises.instruction: Form the correct noun from the adjective.
exercises.text: "Economic ___ has grown in most developed countries." (equal — opposite with -ity → inequality)", (use "inequality")
"Many industries have been ___d, moving from state to private ownership." (private)
"___ studies how governments should manage the economy." (economy)", (which noun?)
"Market ___ occur when unregulated markets produce poor social outcomes." (fail)", (failure)
"The ___ of wages is one of the most debated economic issues." (regulate)", (noun)
"An ___ studies the economy and advises governments on policy." (economy)", (person who studies it)
exercises.hint: economy → economist (-ist suffix: specialist in a field)

exercises.text: "The ___ of the industry improved after new technology was introduced." (produce + -ivity)", (noun)
exercises.hint: productive → productivity (-ity suffix: the quality/state of being productive)

exercises.instruction: Convert the adjective to a verb.
exercises.text: "Governments ___ the currency by printing too much money." (stable → opposite of stable → destabilise/inflate)", (use: inflate)
exercises.hint: inflate = to increase money supply causing inflation; inflate → inflation

exercises.text: "The government decided to ___ the industry to make it more competitive." (liberal)", (verb)
exercises.hint: liberal → liberalise (-ise suffix: to make liberal/free)

exercises.text: "___ of goods across borders has increased dramatically." (distribute — the activity of distributing)", (= distribution)
"The ___ performance of a company determines its share price." (finance → adjective)
exercises.hint: finance → financial (-ial suffix: relating to finance)

exercises.instruction: Form the correct noun from the adjective.
exercises.text: "There is great ___ in the labour market — workers can change jobs easily." (flexible + -ibility → flexibility)", (noun)
exercises.hint: flexible → flexibility (-ity suffix: the state of being flexible)

questions.text: "The ___ of wealth between the rich and poor is highly unequal." (distribute → noun)
"___ in technology companies has grown rapidly." (invest → noun)
"An ___ is a person who studies the economy and economic policy." (economy → person)
questions.hint: economy → economist (-ist: specialist in a field)

questions.text: "Strong ___ between companies keeps prices low and quality high." (compete → noun)
"The government decided to ___ the state-owned airline." (private → verb)
questions.hint: private → privatise (-ise suffix: to make private)
"Economy" (the system) and "economist" (a person) are both nouns

questions.text: "Market ___ occurs when unregulated markets produce suboptimal outcomes." (fail → noun: failure)
"Rising ___ means workers produce more per hour worked." (productive → noun)
"The ___ of wages is fiercely debated between governments and trade unions." (regulate → noun: regulation)
"The ___ of income matters as much as its level." (distribute → noun)
"___ studies how people make decisions under conditions of scarcity." (economy → the discipline)
questions.hint: economy → economics (the discipline; also: the economist studies it)

questions.text: "The government plans to ___ the currency by pegging it to the euro." (stable → verb)
questions.hint: stable → stabilise (-ise suffix: to make stable)
